title: introduce-helix-attention-accelerator-fused-rope-continuous-kv-batcher
author: Arnav Patel
body:
Summary: Introduces the Helix attention accelerator kernel and scheduler integration: a fused rope/rotary path plus a continuous-KV batcher and lightweight prefetcher. This change aims to reduce tail latency for mixed-sequence workloads and decrease per-token compute by improving locality and reducing memory traffic.

Motivation: Production traffic shows increased variance in small/medium sequence mixes (<=1024) where kernel dispatch and KV cache thrashing drive 95th percentile latency spikes. Existing fused kernels were efficient for long homogeneous sequences but did not optimize the small-batch, mixed-length SLOs we primarily serve. Helix focuses on three axes: 1) a compact fused kernel that applies rotary/rope transforms in-register and coalesces QKV writes to reduce memory bandwidth; 2) a continuous-KV batcher that keeps warm KV lanes resident and opportunistically batches across requests while honoring latency SLOs; 3) a predictive KV prefetcher that leverages a lightweight LRU+freq table to warm likely upcoming KV segments.

Changeset highlights:
- runtime/kernels/helix_attn.cu: new CUDA kernel with interleaved QKV fusion, in-place rotary application, and warp-aware tiling. Micro-optimizations: fused GEMM+softmax path for small heads, reduced shared memory copies, and 16-bit accumulation option for fp16 models.
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: scheduler integration that implements continuous batching with SLO-aware delay windows and per-model batching policies.
- runtime/kv/prefetcher.cpp: predictive prefetcher with LRU+freq heuristics and metrics hooks.
- runtime/kv/kv_cache.h/.cpp: API additions to pin/unpin KV lanes and expose temperature metrics.
- tools/bench/helix_microbench.py: microbench harness and a simple latency histogram reporter.
- docs/perf/helix_design.md: architecture notes and configuration knobs (ENV_HELIX_*).

Benchmarks: Microbench on p4d.24xlarge-equivalent machines using a mixed workload (30% tokens <=128, 50% tokens 128-512, 20% tokens 512-1024):
- median latency: -12% vs baseline fused kernel
- p50: 9.8ms -> 8.6ms
- p95 latency: -28% vs baseline fused kernel
- p95: 42ms -> 30.2ms
- throughput (tokens/sec): +6% at 99% SLO compliance

Notes: results vary by model size and head count; improvements are strongest for models with <=32 heads and batch sizes 4-16.

Compatibility and fallbacks: Helix registers as a capability and is automatically selected when model config meets quantization/attention shape constraints. If kernel selection fails, runtime falls back to the prior fused kernel path. The prefetcher is enabled per-model via config; default conservative heuristics are used to avoid regressing memory pressure.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for KV pin/unpin and prefetch heuristics.
- Added end-to-end smoke tests in perf CI.
- Ran a 72-hour canary on Dedicated slice d-helix-01 with production traffic shaping; no regressions observed, observed consistent reduction in retries.

Review and discussion (high-level):
- Initial implementation landed as draft after microbench showed promising median improvements but had outliers in p99 under adversarial request patterns.
- Reviewer requests: Sana asked for hard SLO guards in the scheduler (implemented: per-route max delay window and immediate fallback). Luis requested more telemetry around KV lane temperature and eviction counters (added metrics and console dashboard link in PR body). Julee requested a memory safety audit and we added bounds checks and a small fuzz harness for the prefetcher.

CI and iteration:
- First CI run (linux-gcc-ubuntu/build+unit) failed due to a static initialization order issue in the prefetcher; fixed in second commit.
- perf CI initially showed a 2% regression in throughput for a single large-model synthetic test; root cause was aggressive prefetching on large sequences; added model-size-based heuristic and re-ran.
- Final CI status: all checks passed, microbench and e2e smoke green.

Commits (summary):
- feat(helix): add helix_attn CUDA kernel with interleaved qkv and in-register rotary
- feat(scheduler): continuous KV batcher SLO-aware windowing
- feat(kv): prefetcher with LRU+freq and KV pin/unpin API
- test: helix microbench and kv unit tests
- fix: init order and prefetch heuristic tuning

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/kernels/helix_attn.cu
- runtime/kernels/helix_attn.h
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.h
- runtime/kv/prefetcher.cpp
- runtime/kv/prefetcher.h
- runtime/kv/kv_cache.cpp
- runtime/kv/kv_cache.h
- tools/bench/helix_microbench.py
- tools/profiling/helix_trace_converter.py
- docs/perf/helix_design.md
- ci/perf-config/helix_canary.yaml
- tests/kv/prefetch_tests.cpp
- tests/attn/helix_attn_smoke.cpp

Review thread excerpts:
- Sana Kapoor (reviewer): "Can we bound the batching window per-route by default? Risk is that continuous batching adds latency for latency-sensitive routes." Author reply: "Added per-route max_delay_ms config (ENV_HELIX_MAX_DELAY_MS) and default 8ms; updated docs and tests."
- Luis Moreno (reviewer): "Add metrics for kv_lane_temperature and eviction_count and expose via tracing hooks." Author reply: "Added gauge and counter, updated console dashboard link in docs."
- Julee Park (reviewer): "Please run a memory safety pass and add assertions for index math in the kernel." Author reply: "Added bounds checks in kernel and a small fuzz harness; no issues found."

CI summary:
- linux-build: pass
- unit-tests: pass
- perf-microbench: pass
- canary-deploy: pass

Merge: Squash-merged into main. Merge commit: "squash: helix attn accelerator + continuous kv batcher (Closes ENG-5421)"

Rollout plan and release notes:
- Rollout: start with Dedicated Canary d-helix-01, then expand to low-traffic hosts, followed by gradual ramp to 50% of hosted API within 2 weeks.
- Release notes: "Add Helix attention accelerator: fused rope/rotary kernel, continuous KV batcher, and predictive KV prefetcher. Improves p95 latency on mixed-length workloads by up to 28% and reduces per-token compute for small/medium sequences. Enabled via ENV_HELIX_ENABLED=true."
